title: Recover ambiguous payment state without a duplicate effect

state.summary: A payment mutation was dispatched, its acknowledgement was lost, and authoritative commit state is unknown.
known_facts: One logical payment operation identity exists.
constraints: Do not create a new payment mutation while authoritative commit state is unknown.

tension.summary: The system must continue without guessing whether the first financial mutation committed.

cause.summary: Transport ambiguity separates mutation dispatch from authoritative knowledge of the committed outcome.
cause.basis: The completed DRP decision requires authoritative state recovery before another financial mutation.

confidence_assessment.rationale: The provider-neutral fixture explicitly records a lost acknowledgement and unknown commit state.
alternative_explanations: The original mutation committed despite the lost acknowledgement.
The original mutation did not commit.

transition.trigger: authoritative transaction lookup using the existing payment operation identity
transition.expected_consequence: Recover the existing transaction outcome without creating a second payment effect.

participants.name: human intent owner
participants.risk: A blind retry could create a duplicate charge.

participants.name: payment recovery controller
participants.goal: Continue only from authoritative state evidence.
participants.risk: Guessing commit state could authorize the wrong transition.

cooperation.shared_upside: The workflow continues from evidence while preserving the original one-payment intent.

action.summary: Read authoritative transaction state for the existing payment operation before authorizing any new financial mutation.
action.review_after: after authoritative lookup returns a terminal or still-unknown result

review.summary: Authoritative lookup found the original operation committed; no second payment mutation was issued.
review.actual_consequence: One existing payment effect was accepted and a duplicate mutation was avoided.
